Compare two provenance receipts

Source: R/crt_receipt_compare.R
crt_receipt_compare.Rd

Judges a rebuild against its reference copy and answers with one of three verdicts, naming every field that differed (crate#43):

Usage

crt_receipt_compare(a, b, tables = NULL, keys = NULL)

Arguments

a, b

Receipts, as lists from crt_receipt_read(), or paths to them. a is the reference copy.

tables

Optional: list(a = list(<table> = <data frame>), b = list(...)), the two builds' tables to re-read.

keys

Optional: the package's declaration, from crt_receipt_keys(), whose register overrides the default action for fields outside the recipe.

Value

A list of class crt_receipt_comparison: verdict; mode, "receipts" or "bytes"; and differences, a tibble with one row per field that differed: side (output, recipe, result or context), field, action (refuse, warn, record, or within for a difference inside its tolerance), and detail; register, the version of the register the verdict was judged under; and overrides, the action the declaration in keys gave each field whose action it changed, named by field (empty when it changed none). It lists every such field, whether or not that field differed in this comparison.

Details

  • identical: the same recipe and the same result.

  • equivalent: the same recipe, and every result value that differs is within the tolerance the output declares.

  • different: another recipe, or a result value past its tolerance.

What a difference in each field does comes from the receipt register (inst/extdata/receipt/register/v1.0.0/register.csv, published at https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/crate/receipt/register/v1.0.0/register.csv), one row per field: refuse makes the verdict different, warn is reported without changing it, and record is listed only. Every recipe field refuses, because recipe_id covers it; every context field is recorded, because the machine and the toolchain are never part of an identity.

A verdict is a function of the register's rows, so the register is versioned on its own (crate#58) and every comparison names the version it was judged under. A row change is a new register version; it never moves the version a receipt carries, which is its form's.

Receipts or bytes

A comparison of receipts alone compares what the writers claimed. A table whose fingerprints differ is then different, even when the difference is a value that rounded the other way at the edge of its tolerance (0.0000000014 and 0.0000000016 under 1e-9). Supply both builds' tables and the comparison re-reads them: it checks each against its own receipt's fingerprint, then compares their cells, and a table whose cells all agree within tolerance is equivalent. The result's mode says which was done.

A file whose bytes differ is equivalent only when its receipt names the table it holds (parts, named, in crt_receipt_write()) and that table agrees; a file that names no table, such as a raster nobody fingerprinted, is different.

Examples

wc <- system.file("extdata", "receipt", "examples", "worked_case", package = "crate")
crt_receipt_compare(file.path(wc, "build_1"), file.path(wc, "build_2"))
#> equivalent (receipts only; register v1.0.0)
#>   within result.parts[access_check.csv].bytes: 124 vs 128; table access_check agrees
#>   within result.parts[access_check.csv].sha256: "04994ff01cdee55d69fc410add51ad261ec4b33a751135fc224e97305823c3e2" vs "6801fb7bb092626441fd804d5ffbf8c4c05213ff18fa7c7ca524a9c2aa32f5e4"; table access_check agrees
#>   within result.summary[km_total]: 47.3767792597 vs 47.376779259805; within 1e-06
#>   record context.run: {"link_run_id":"20261104T181900Z-bulk"} vs {"link_run_id":"20261104T214400Z-bulk"}
#>   record context.time: "2026-11-04T18:22:05Z" vs "2026-11-04T21:47:31Z"
